data.long_meaning: Deva (god) + Neeth (gift). This name is derived from Sanskrit and is associated with the divine blessings of the gods. Devaneeth is a name that signifies the bestowal of divine grace and blessings upon a child. The name Devaneeth carries the meaning “God's gift” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Devaneeth usually hope their child will grow to embody god's gift and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.cultural_impact: The name Devaneeth carries with it deep cultural significance in Hindu tradition. The prefix "Deva" symbolizes the divine, and the suffix "Neeth" means "gift." Devaneeth thus represents a gift from the gods, a child blessed by the divine. This name is revered in Hindu families as a symbol of divine favor and protection. It has been traditionally given to boys to acknowledge their special, god-given status, although it can also be given to girls.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Devaneeth holds deep significance as it indicates a connection to the divine realm. It signifies that the individual carrying this name is a recipient of divine grace and blessings. The name is a reminder of the presence of God in one's life and the ongoing support and guidance of the divine. Devaneeth serves as a constant inspiration to lead a virtuous and god-centered life.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Devaneeth: God's grace and blessings embodied. The divine essence within an individual.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Devanéethi Chola (or Devanātha Chola) was a Chola king who ruled from 1153 to 1163 CE. The name Devaneeth carried significant spiritual weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Devanéethi Chola was an important ruler during the later Chola Empire in Tamil Nadu, India. He is known to have made several temple constructions and endowments, and his reign was marked by peace and prosperity.

historical_references.reference: Devanéetha Perumal is the name of a Hindu deity venerated in the Divya Desam temples. It is believed that Lord Vishnu appeared before sage Agastya in the form of Devanéetha Perumal during the Treta Yuga.
historical_references.context: Devanéetha Perumal is a form of Lord Vishnu, and is believed to have appeared before the sage Agastya during the Treta Yuga, an epoch in Hindu mythology. The name Devanéetha means 'the one who protects the gods', and the form of Lord Vishnu in this name is often depicted with a discus, a conch shell, and a mace, symbols of his divine power.
